title: Peer pressure and social influence
examples: What is the difference between wanting to fit in and wanting to be yourself?
How does social media affect our need to fit in with friends?

explain.say: Today we are learning about how friends and groups can influence us.

items: Groups can affect our thoughts and actions.
We often want to be liked by others.

explain.say: Conformity means matching your behaviour to a group.
The Asch experiment showed how strong group pressure can be.
A key finding was that people often agree even when they know better.
Learning to say no is a powerful skill for your independence.
In real life, you might feel pressured to buy something you do not need.

faq.q: Why do we feel the need to agree with the group?
faq.a: Humans have a natural desire to belong to a group. Being accepted helps us feel safe and connected.
asks: Why is fitting in so important?
What makes us want to follow others?

faq.q: Does being different always cause problems with friends?
faq.a: Not always. True friends value you for who you are, even if you disagree with them sometimes.
asks: Is it bad to have different opinions?
How can I be myself around new people?

faq.q: What is the main lesson from the Asch experiment?
faq.a: The experiment showed that even when the answer is obvious, the desire to fit in can make us say something incorrect.
asks: Did the people know the right answer?

faq.q: What does it mean to be assertive when saying no?
faq.a: It means stating your refusal clearly and calmly while still respecting others.
asks: How do I say no without arguing?
Is being firm the same as being rude?

faq.q: Are there times when following the group is actually helpful?
faq.a: Yes, groups help us learn rules and safety procedures, like crossing the road together.
asks: Can groups help us learn new skills?

facts: Conformity is the act of changing your beliefs or behaviour to match a group.
The Asch experiment involved judging the length of lines.
Saying no clearly is an important part of building self-respect.
Social influence can be positive, helping us learn good habits.

quiz.say: When people agree with a group even when they know it is wrong, this is called:
quiz.why: Conformity is the specific term for matching behaviour to a group's expectations.

wrong.1: Agreement is just saying yes; conformity describes the reason for the agreement.
wrong.2: Socializing is the general act of spending time with people, not the pressure to match them.
wrong.3: Peer acceptance is the goal, but conformity is the action taken to achieve it.

quiz.say: If you feel pressured to do something unsafe, what is the best first step?

options.show: Wait for someone else to speak.
options.say: Wait for someone else to speak.

quiz.why: Walking away removes you from the immediate source of pressure, giving you space to think.

wrong.0: Agreeing even briefly can make it harder to refuse later.
wrong.1: Waiting puts the responsibility on someone else, which is not always reliable.
wrong.3: Arguing can make the situation more confrontational and stressful.

quiz.say: If a friend pressures you to skip class, and you decide to politely refuse and leave with another friend, you are demonstrating:
quiz.why: Assertiveness means stating your needs clearly while respecting the other person.

wrong.1: Conformity means giving in to the group's wishes, which is the opposite of what you did.
wrong.2: Submission means letting others control your actions without speaking up for yourself.
wrong.3: Conflict is the fight itself; assertiveness is the skill you use to manage the disagreement.
